blockers.finding: The corrected entry reads: '...the binding product packet records CD-RT-5 DECIDED 2026-08-05, and the retained checker's own RC-14 finding text is machine proof of the decided state'. The first conjunct is true and correctly cited to the constitutive authority. The second is false as stated. RC-14 (check-retention-custody.py _authority_guard) reads product-dispositions.v1.json#pendingDecisions.CD-RT-5.status and fires when that value is not BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A; the live packet's pendingDecisions is the empty object, so the read returns None and the finding text says 'got None'. None is produced identically by decision, deletion, withdrawal, or restructuring -- the finding text cannot distinguish them, and the checker never reads $.decisions.CD-RT-5, where the DECIDED state actually lives. The finding text is therefore machine proof that the blocked row LEFT the packet's pending section -- exactly how the v12 review put it ('the checker fails precisely BECAUSE the blocked state left the live corpus') -- and not machine proof of the decided state. Under this corpus's standard (7.2.2: measurements get hard comparison; 7.2.2.1: a false disclosure spends the reader's trust; the restatement-authorship doctrine that blocked EV12-IR-05 one generation ago), a corroboration that teaches absence-of-a-row as proof of a specific successor state is the EV12-IR-04 pattern -- true facts joined to an evidentiary frame the measurement does not support -- in the exact leaf under repair.
